Usage: comicraft [--fullscreen] <comic.cbz | comic.cbr | comic.pdf | folder>
       comicraft tag <comic> [--<field> <value>...]         its ComicInfo.xml
       comicraft tag <comic | folder> --lookup [--rename]   filled in from Metron
       comicraft convert <comic | folder> [--format pdf]    a CBZ or PDF of it
       comicraft forget <comic> | --all                     where you were in it

A comic opens where you left it, on its page, fitted and zoomed as it was.
Given a folder, ComiCraft shows the comics in it, to choose one to read.
'comicraft tag --help', 'convert --help' and 'forget --help' say more.

Keys:
  Space, Page Down      a screen across or down, then the next page
  Page Up               a screen back across or up, then the page before
  Down, Up              down or up a little, then on or back a page
  Right, Left           a little across a wide page, else turn the page
  Backspace             previous page
  Home, End             first page, last page
  W                     fit the page whole, or to the width
  +, -  (or =)          zoom in, zoom out
  0                     the whole page again
  I                     comic details on and off
  L, Tab                the comics in the folder on and off
  F, F11                full screen on and off
  Escape                put details away, or quit
  Q                     quit

The mouse wheel scrolls a page that is larger than the window, across and
down; with Ctrl, or as a pinch on a trackpad, it zooms at the pointer. A
drag moves the page. A click on the right half of the window goes forward,
as Page Down does, and on the left half back; with the details showing, a
click puts them away.

A page larger than the window is read across, then down. Where a page fits
the window, every key that goes on or back turns a page.

In the comics in the folder, Up and Down (and Page Up, Page Down, Home and
End) choose one; Enter or Right opens it, or goes into a folder, and Left or
Backspace goes up a folder. A click
[truncated]

Usage: comicraft tag <comic>
       comicraft tag <comic> --<field> <value>... [--convert] [--delete-original | --keep-original]
       comicraft tag <comic | folder> --lookup [--rename] ...   ('tag --lookup --help' says more)

With no fields, shows the comic's ComicInfo.xml. With fields, changes them: a field given
an empty value ("") is removed. Field names are ComicInfo's, in any case, with or without
hyphens: --series, --cover-artist, --CoverArtist. --field=value works too.

A CBR cannot be changed, only converted to a CBZ that can. You are asked whether to
convert it, unless --convert is given; and then whether to move the original to the
Trash, unless --delete-original or --keep-original is. Run from a script, nothing is
asked: a CBR is not converted without --convert, and an original is kept without
--delete-original. An original the Trash will not take is only deleted permanently
when you say so; a script keeps it.

Fields:
  Title, Series, Number, Count, Volume, AlternateSeries, AlternateNumber,
  AlternateCount, Summary, Notes, Year, Month, Day, Writer, Penciller, Inker, Colorist,
  Letterer, CoverArtist, Editor, Translator, Publisher, Imprint, Genre, Tags, Web,
  PageCount, LanguageISO, Format, BlackAndWhite, Manga, Characters, Teams, Locations,
  ScanInformation, StoryArc, StoryArcNumber, SeriesGroup, AgeRating, CommunityRating,
  MainCharacterOrTeam, Review, GTIN.

Usage: comicraft convert <comic> [--format cbz | pdf] [--to <file>] [--delete-original | --keep-original]
       comicraft convert <folder> [--format cbz | pdf] [--from <kinds>] [--recursive]
                                  [--delete-original | --keep-original]

Makes a CBZ of the comic, or, with --format pdf, a PDF, beside it by the same name, or at
the file --to names; a --to that ends in .pdf makes a PDF without --format. An existing
file is never written over.

A CBZ has everything that is in the comic. A PDF has its pages, a page of the PDF to each,
and its ComicInfo.xml, which goes in as an attachment and gives the PDF its title and
author. Nothing is lost: JPEG and PNG pages go in as they are, and WebP, GIF and BMP
pages as their pixels. A PDF whose pages are pictures converts to a CBZ of them, as
they are, with its ComicInfo.xml.

Given a folder, converts every CBR in it to a CBZ, or, with --format pdf, every CBR and
CBZ to a PDF, each beside itself; with --recursive, those in the folders in it too.
--from says which kinds to convert instead: cbr, cbz or pdf, or more than one, as in
--from cbr,pdf; so --from pdf converts every PDF to a CBZ. A comic whose CBZ or PDF is
already there is skipped, and one that cannot be converted is reported, and the rest go
on. Ctrl+C stops once the comic being converted is done.

Afterwards, you are asked whether to move the original to the Trash (for a folder, once,
before any is converted); the answer is no unless it is yes. --delete-original and
--keep-original answer before it is asked, as a script must. An original only goes once
what was made has been read back and found to have its pages. An original the Trash will
not take is only deleted permanently when you say so; a script, or a folder, keeps it.

Usage: comicraft forget <comic>
       comicraft forget --all

A comic opens where you left it: at the page you were on, fitted, zoomed and scrolled as
it was. forget forgets where you were in the comic, which then opens at its first page,
as it did the first time; the comic need not be there any more. --all forgets every comic.

Where you were is kept in /tmp/inspectra-help-comicr-747106d8-d93d47ce/home/.local/state/comicraft/reading.json,
for the last 1000 comics read. Nothing else is kept there.
